kind: tool comparison (TLSF), 2x2 factorial, all four arms from one binary, run at AuRUS's own search budget; a repeat of 2026-08-29-aurus-matched at the engine main carries after PR #171
kind_note: The same design as 2026-08-29-aurus-matched, run again because four commits moved the search path between that campaign's binary and main: the equivalence collapse in the implication filter (4ad290d), the final-filter simplify skip (1330f13), and the maximal and compare simplify skips (d4f8be4, 11305f9). The earlier campaign's result was also depressed by a 10.5% kill rate at the 7200 s cap that the final-filter speedup was expected to reduce. It did, to 6.4%. Both campaigns are reported whatever the outcome; PLAN.md section 5 says so and experiments/README.md carries the supersession row.
question: Whether counter's registered cell, nsga2-apportion with mrs grading, repairs to the ideal more or less often than AuRUS per family when both search 1000 individuals, at the engine main carries; and, as secondaries, what the selection scheme and the status grading cost inside that budget and what the anytime curves look like.
endpoint: Registered in PLAN.md section 4: per-family implies_ideal rate, nsga2-apportion/mrs against AuRUS, exact two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank over the 25 families at alpha 0.05, a killed run counting as a failure on both sides. The secondary read drops the killed runs on both sides. The pooled head-to-head over the four cells, the 2x2 contrasts and every per-family number are secondary and carry no rule (section 5).
decision_rule_firing: Outcome 3, null, reported as parity. Over 25 families counter's registered cell is higher on 12, lower on 8 and tied on 5, mean difference -0.053, exact two-sided Wilcoxon p = 0.7216. The registered secondary over scorable runs only reads 23 families, counter higher on 11, lower on 7, tied on 5, mean difference -0.020, p = 0.9238. Neither reading crosses alpha, so neither outcome 1 nor outcome 2 fires, and the secondary is reported beside the primary rather than in its place. 2026-08-29-aurus-matched read the pooled contrast null as well (p = 0.2896 counting kills, p = 0.5392 over scorable runs), and the 2026-08-21 ship campaign read it null at counter's own budget (p = 0.7549); this is the third null on the contrast and the first with a registered cell and rule. The p-values under the 2x2 and the pooled head-to-head in REPORT.md are secondary by registration, not post-hoc by omission as the earlier archive's were.

arms.shared: termination individuals, max_individuals 1000, generations 500 (ceiling), population_size 100, parallel 1, weights 0.1/0.2/0.7, log metric, weakening screen off, accumulate_repairs on, monolithic repair mode, --pin-vintage; the aurus-matched generator line unchanged but for the output directory

binary_commit.source: counter --version, read by run_experiments.py at startup and stamped onto every row

hosts.note: The seed split comes from campaign.toml alone and was never chosen at a prompt; both phases were enqueued together and the tick ran them in order (see deviations.calibration_gate_unenforced). The split is over seeds and never over the factors, so both arms of every within-counter contrast ran on one host and a host difference cancels inside the (spec, seed) cell. Both hosts started the main phase within the same second and finished 18 minutes apart.

rows.collected_with: campaign.py collect --csv results-rematch.csv --results-dir results-rematch on 2026-09-07, the rematch profiles existing only on the branch and so absent from merge_experiments.PROFILE_CSVS; verified as a union of the two hosts' 1500-row files.

calibration_phase.design: six families (humanoid-742, humanoid-531, pcar-v2-888, full-arbiter-aurus, minepump, rg2) at one seed a host across all four cells, PLAN.md section 7
calibration_phase.note: Its rows sit in results-rematch-calib.csv beside the archive and enter no figure in REPORT.md; the main phase's own rows are the record. Its run directories are what the maximality pass was calibrated on (see maximality_pass.calibration).

verification.note: The five checks the analysis runs before anything is drawn from the rows, carried over from the aurus-matched plan's section 12; analysis-output.txt holds the printout.

1_stopped_by.detail: individuals on all 2807 manifests, generations on none. The 500-generation ceiling never bound.

2_individuals_bred.detail: Exactly 1000 on every one of the 2807 manifests. Zero overshoot.

3_ideal_solutions_join.detail: implies_ideal is 1431 of 3000 (47.7%) in the results CSV and the curve join reads ideal_solutions > 0 on 1527 of 2999 runs; the two sources agree that the endpoint is not flat zero. The curve count exceeds the CSV count because a killed run has curves and no verdict.

4_cost_off_own_rows.result: 0.68x the archive on the same design
4_cost_off_own_rows.detail: Mean 944.2 s a run against the archive's 1382.5 s, median 156 s against 296 s, max 7200.1 s. 786.8 core-hours against 1152.1. The plan's section 10 carried the archive figure as an upper bound and it held.

5_censored_count.result: 192 directories of 3000 (6.4%) hold accumulated/index.tsv and no run.json; 193 rows read timed_out
5_censored_count.detail: Concentrated: humanoid-742 107/120, humanoid-531 56/120, pcar-v2-888 10/120, prioritized-arbiter-aurus 10/120, humanoid-503 8/120, lift 1/120. The archive read 315 (10.5%), with humanoid-742 on 120/120 and humanoid-531 on 93/120. The one row beyond the 192 directories is a humanoid-503 weighted/aurus run that left no accumulated directory at all. humanoid-742 still caps on 107 of 120, so the question PLAN.md section 7 says the calibration turns on is answered: the speedup reached humanoid-531 (93 to 56) and pcar-v2-888 (44 to 10) and left humanoid-742 largely where it was.

cost.note: 49.1% of the machine time went on runs killed at the 7200 s cap, against 54.7% in the archive. A killed run writes no manifest and scores as a failure in every column of the results CSV, so that share bought no scored row; only the accumulator, which flushes as it goes, records what those runs found.

section_11_measures.note: The six per-arm measures the aurus-matched plan's section 11 named, read off results-rematch.csv; the archive's values are beside them in REPORT.md.

registered_primary.largest_differences: counter ahead on full-arbiter-aurus (+0.567, AuRUS 0 of 30 with 9 kills), prioritized-arbiter-aurus (+0.433, AuRUS 0 of 30 with 24 kills) and humanoid-531 (+0.200); behind on humanoid-742 (-0.933, counter 0 of 30 with 30 kills), gyro-var2 (-0.633), lily11 (-0.533) and lift (-0.367). humanoid-742 and humanoid-503 drop out of the scorable read, one side of each having no scorable run.

selection_nsga2_apportion_vs_weighted.found_repair: nsga2-apportion only 116, weighted only 28, exact McNemar p < 0.0001
selection_nsga2_apportion_vs_weighted.implies_ideal: nsga2-apportion only 135, weighted only 72, exact McNemar p < 0.0001
selection_nsga2_apportion_vs_weighted.wall: nsga2-apportion faster on 1366 of 1500; means 653.3 s against 1235.1 s

grading_mrs_vs_aurus.found_repair: mrs only 62, aurus only 38, exact McNemar p = 0.0210
grading_mrs_vs_aurus.implies_ideal: mrs only 95, aurus only 84, exact McNemar p = 0.4549
grading_mrs_vs_aurus.wall: mrs faster on 629 of 1500; means 1067.2 s against 821.3 s

factor_contrasts_secondary.note: Both contrasts point the way the archive's did. The selection contrast is the sharper of the two and the grading contrast on implies_ideal is null again; mrs now clears aurus on found_repair where the archive read p = 0.0798.

per_family_implies_ideal.note: humanoid-742 nsga2-apportion/aurus is the one cell that moved by more than a few runs against the archive, 0/30 to 13/30: its runs in that cell now finish under the cap where every one of the archive's was killed. The registered cell, nsga2-apportion/mrs, still caps on all 30 there.

deviations.calibration_gate_unenforced: PLAN.md section 7 gates the main phase on the calibration's extrapolated cost. Both phases were enqueued together and the tick runs a declaration's phases in order without pausing, so main followed calib whatever the calibration said. Recorded in the plan's 2026-09-04 amendment (0dd5da6) before any row existed. The ceiling given up was the archive's 1152.1 core-hours; the campaign cost 786.8.
deviations.aurus_arm_reused_not_rerun: PLAN.md section 9 re-runs the AuRUS arm in the same window and screens its output for well-separation. It was not run. On 2026-09-07 the decision was taken to score the primary against the archived AuRUS reference rows instead, experiments/aurus-reference/ as 2026-08-29-aurus-matched used them, because the changes between the two campaigns were made to counter alone and nothing about AuRUS, its corpus, its settings or its hosts moved. The three reasons section 3 gave for re-running the arm were the shared window, the well-separation screen and a fresh sample; the first two are given up, the third was never a requirement of the test. Consequences that stand: the AuRUS rates are unfiltered for well-separation, as the archive's were, and the two sides remain scored by different standards on that one property; and AuRUS's 72 lost-at-cap runs carry no verdict, so its rate on humanoid-503 is over 0 scorable runs and that family drops out of the scorable read.
deviations.maximal_timeout_not_raised: PLAN.md section 8 item 3 says to raise --maximal-timeout if partial curves survive the calibration at the fast binary. They did, 12 of 46, and the budget was kept at 900 s after a measurement rather than raised: see maximality_pass.calibration.doubled_budget_measurement. --compare-timeout was raised, as item 3's last paragraph says to.

caveats.aurus_rates_are_unfiltered: As in the archive: the well-separation screen's inputs did not survive, so AuRUS's per-family rates count every ideal-implying solution and counter's output gate rejects an ill-separated survivor unconditionally. The archived record of the screen is that it moved 2 of 25 family rates, lift 0.167 to 0.300 and lily11 0.900 to 0.833.
caveats.a_kill_is_not_symmetric: counter's accumulator flushes as it goes, so a killed counter run keeps its candidates and its curves but scores implies_ideal as a failure; AuRUS writes its solutions when the run ends, so a killed AuRUS run carries no verdict and drops out. humanoid-742 reads 0.000 for the registered cell on 30 kills against AuRUS's 0.933, and humanoid-503 has no scorable AuRUS run at all. The plan registers the kill-as-failure read as primary and the scorable read as secondary, and REPORT.md gives both.
caveats.solution_means_two_things: counter's curve counts gate-passing candidates with sub-second timestamps; AuRUS's counts accepted solutions read off a per-iteration log line dated to the second. Read the two at the coarser resolution.
caveats.curves_not_comparable_to_the_archive: 4ad290d collapses mutually equivalent specifications in the implication filter, which shrinks the candidate set the maximality pass sees, and the pass ran under different compare and deadline budgets from the archive's. Curve values here and in 2026-08-29-aurus-matched are not put in one table.
caveats.paper_gaps: Unchanged from the archive: counter matches AuRUS's code rather than its paper on the weights, the six-level status ladder and how an individual is counted, so no claim here may be made against the paper's Table 2.

scoring_binaries.note: One binary for every curve, as PLAN.md section 8 item 1 requires: maximal and compare were built from f8fbe26 on both hosts, read back through --version before the pass and recorded in maximal.version and compare.version beside the per-run files. Both carry the simplify skip (d4f8be4 for maximal, 11305f9 for compare), so no curve here was scored under the ltlfilt --simplify pass the archive's 1956 old-build curves were.

maximality_pass.invocation: scripts/score_curves.py --maximality --cuts 20 --jobs 4 --maximal-timeout 900 --compare-timeout <CMPT> --deadline-s <DEADLINE>, one invocation per run directory under an outer timeout of DEADLINE + 900 s, eight workers a host over a smallest-first queue by accumulated/index.tsv length, each worker pinned to four cores with taskset; av2 scored seeds 0-14 and av3 seeds 15-29, the campaign's own split. The budgets were read from a flags file at each invocation and each run's timings line records the three it ran under.
maximality_pass.mechanism: Hand-rolled, as the archive's was: two shell scripts on each host, a Monitor in the closing session watching for completion, and this block assembled by hand from the timings, failures and version files afterwards. campaign.py had no phase kind for a scoring pass, which is the gap the owed entry names; the pass was not moved onto the new mechanism mid-flight.

worker_hours.note: 0.44x the archive's pass on the same design, with compare and deadline budgets several times larger. Wall clock was 20.1 h a host over eight workers.

budgets.history: The pass launched at the plan's 900/600/4500 (maximal/compare/deadline). The calibration pass had shown compare exceeding 600 s on humanoid-742 weighted runs, and two unbounded compare calls on calibration directories of that family measured 1590 s (258 relations) and 1324 s (319), so the flags file was raised to 900/3000/7500 about an hour into the main pass, before the queue reached any run of the affected families. The 647 runs scored under the first budgets are the smallest in the queue, 327 on av2 and 320 on av3, costing 14.0 worker-hours between them; every run of humanoid-742, humanoid-531, pcar-v2-888, humanoid-503 and prioritized-arbiter-aurus ran under the second.

calibration.runs: 46 of the 48 calibration-phase run directories, scored at 900/600/4500 on 2026-09-07 before the main pass; the two aurus/weighted humanoid-531 runs were still in flight when the main pass was launched and were not scored
calibration.against_the_archive: 36,182 worker-seconds against the archive's 79,881 over the 39 of those runs the archive's own pass had timed, 2.2x faster at the one binary; PLAN.md section 8 item 2 said to expect a large speedup and not assume it, and this is the measurement.
calibration.compare_undecided: 4 of 46, all humanoid-742 weighted, which is what raised the compare budget
calibration.doubled_budget_measurement: Two of the 12 partial calibration curves were re-scored at --maximal-timeout 1800 --deadline-s 7200 to price item 3 of section 8. pcar-v2-888 mrs/weighted seed 0 reached 10 cuts in 4431 s against 9 in 1999 s; humanoid-742 mrs/nsga2-apportion seed 1 reached 4 cuts in 4705 s against 4 in 2629 s. One extra cut on one run and none on the other, for about twice the cost. A cut that exceeds 900 s exceeds 1800 s too, the late cuts' batch size being what drives the cost, so the per-cut budget was kept at 900 s and the partial curves are read as undecided past their last cut, as the archive's are. The survivor-block skip in owed is what would move them.

partial_curves.share: 9.1% of 3000, 9.3% of the 2932 runs with a maximal curve
partial_curves.meaning: score_curves.py abandons a cut whose maximal call exceeds the 900 s per-cut budget and writes the cuts it has. A partial curve ends before the run's last arrival and carries no marker of its own; analyse_matched.py detects one by that test and reads its cuts past the last computed one as undecided rather than carrying the last value forward. The bracketed count beside each maximal cell in analysis-output.txt is the number of runs so excluded at that cut. The archive read 280.
partial_curves.note: The denominators under by_family are runs with a maximal curve. 68 runs have none because their accumulator is empty: 39 nsga2-apportion/aurus and 29 weighted/aurus, the aurus-graded arms being the ones that fail to find any repair on the hard families.

compare_undecided_runs.run: humanoid-742 seed 11, weighted/mrs, on av2: compare exceeded the 3000 s cap, so its ideal_solutions and maximal_ideal_solutions are blank at every cut and the analysis reports it as undecided
compare_undecided_runs.against_the_archive: 205 in the archive, 118 of humanoid-742's 120 among them. 11305f9 on compare's TLSF path and the 3000 s cap together removed all but this one.
compare_undecided_runs.lower_bound: compare still leaves individual candidate-ideal pairs undecided inside runs it finishes, and an undecided pair counts as not ideal-implying, so every ideal count in the curves is a lower bound. The results CSV's implies_ideal is the run's own gate and is not affected.

maximality_pass.redundant_work_not_removed: As in the archive: each cut re-decides from cold the survivor-against-survivor pairs the previous cut already found non-dominating. Removing them is exact and would roughly halve the pass; it is in owed.

vendored_scripts.note: Verbatim copies, each verified with git hash-object. The four that ran the campaign are as they stood at f8fbe26, the commit the hosts ran; their blobs are unchanged since the commits named beside them. The five that scored and analysed it are taken from d29cfc4, the analysis tip at close, which adds --primary and --runs-dir to analyse_matched.py; score_curves.py is byte-identical to the archive's vendored copy. analysis_lib.py is vendored because analyse_matched.py imports it.

owed: A `score` phase kind in campaign.py, so the maximality pass is declared in campaign.toml, launched and resumed by the tick, gated on the scoring binaries' freshness, and recorded in a per-host manifest this block can be assembled from. Two campaigns have now run the pass by hand, 716.2 and 311.7 worker-hours, each time the whole RQ3 result. In progress on feat/campaign-score-phase at close.

The survivor-block skip in score_curves.py's maximality pass, carried over from the archive: exact, roughly halves the pass, and is what would bring the 273 partial curves within the per-cut budget on every family but humanoid-742. The doubled-budget measurement above is the evidence that raising the budget does not.
A pairwise-relation flag on compare, carried over from the archive, for the incremental antichain.

A re-run of the AuRUS arm with the well-separation screen's inputs kept, as PLAN.md section 9 specified, should the unfiltered-rate caveat ever need closing. Nothing about AuRUS changed, so the archive's rows stand until then.
A re-score of the one compare-undecided run, humanoid-742 seed 11 weighted/mrs, should anything need that family's ideal curve complete; it is one compare call at a longer cap.
config_vintage: No entry is owed in the 'Config vintage' note of experiments/README.md. No C++ default moved for this campaign, and the generator ran with --pin-vintage, so every config states the vintage keys explicitly.

reproduce: Check out f8fbe26, build the release preset, and drive it with this directory's vendored scripts/gen_configs.py using the command campaign.toml carries, then run_experiments.py --profile rematch-calib and --profile rematch over the seed split campaign.toml declares. The AuRUS side is not reproducible from this repository: it is the archived reference in experiments/aurus-reference/, gitignored, extracted from that tool's own archive on av2 by the two vendored aurus scripts.
